def process(worldcities, romanCities) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    wc = worldcities.copy()
    rc = romanCities.copy()

    # Normalize likely latitude/longitude column names
    def find_col(df, candidates):
        cols = {c.lower(): c for c in df.columns}
        for cand in candidates:
            if cand in cols:
                return cols[cand]
        return None

    wc_lat = find_col(wc, ['lat', 'latitude'])
    wc_lng = find_col(wc, ['lng', 'lon', 'longitude'])
    wc_pop = find_col(wc, ['population', 'pop'])

    rc_lat = find_col(rc, ['lat', 'latitude'])
    rc_lng = find_col(rc, ['lng', 'lon', 'longitude'])

    if wc_lat is None or wc_lng is None or wc_pop is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not find required columns in worldcities. Columns: {list(wc.columns)}")
    if rc_lat is None or rc_lng is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not find required columns in romanCities. Columns: {list(rc.columns)}")

    # Coerce numeric
    wc[wc_pop] = pd.to_numeric(wc[wc_pop], errors='coerce')
    wc[wc_lat] = pd.to_numeric(wc[wc_lat], errors='coerce')
    wc[wc_lng] = pd.to_numeric(wc[wc_lng], errors='coerce')
    rc[rc_lat] = pd.to_numeric(rc[rc_lat], errors='coerce')
    rc[rc_lng] = pd.to_numeric(rc[rc_lng], errors='coerce')

    # Filter modern cities >100k population and with coordinates
    wc_f = wc[(wc[wc_pop] > 100_000) & wc[wc_lat].notna() & wc[wc_lng].notna()].copy()
    rc_f = rc[rc[rc_lat].notna() & rc[rc_lng].notna()].copy()

    # Bounding-box join on +/-0.1 degrees in both lat and lon
    wc_f['__key'] = 1
    rc_f['__key'] = 1
    cand = wc_f.merge(rc_f, on='__key', suffixes=('_wc', '_rc')).drop(columns='__key')

    lat_ok = (cand[f'{wc_lat}_wc'] - cand[f'{rc_lat}_rc']).abs() <= 0.1
    lon_ok = (cand[f'{wc_lng}_wc'] - cand[f'{rc_lng}_rc']).abs() <= 0.1
    near = cand[lat_ok & lon_ok]

    # Count DISTINCT modern cities that have at least one nearby roman city
    wc_id = find_col(wc_f, ['id', 'city_ascii', 'city', 'name'])
    # If no identifier column, fall back to unique lat/lon pair
    if wc_id is not None:
        distinct_modern = near[wc_id + '_wc'].dropna().unique()
        count = len(distinct_modern)
    else:
        count = near[[f'{wc_lat}_wc', f'{wc_lng}_wc']].drop_duplicates().shape[0]

    return pd.DataFrame({'count':[int(count)]})
